question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is kept captive for fulfilment of demands of money or conditions.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Hostage"** means a person who is kept captive for the fulfillment of demands of money or conditions. (बंधक)

 
 
• **Example:** The kidnappers took several **hostages** during the bank robbery.
 
 
 
• **"Hostage"** refers to someone held against their will in order to force another party to act in a certain way. (बंधक)
 
 
• **Example:** The rebels held the diplomat **hostage** to negotiate the release of their imprisoned comrades.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct one-word substitute for the given idiom is **'Hostage'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Doyen **(श्रेठतम व्यक्ति): The most respected or prominent person in a particular field.

 
 
• **Example:** He is considered the **doyen** of classical music in our country.
 
 
 
• **Bait **(चारा): Something used to lure someone into a trap or to catch an animal.
 
 
• **Example:** The fisherman used worms as** bait** to catch the fish.
 
 
 
• **Scion** (वंशज): A descendant of a notable family.
 
 
• **Example:** He is a** scion** of the royal family.
